key_themes: Big Tech earnings wave — Alphabet, Tesla, IBM, ServiceNow all reporting Q2 after the close
AI capex surge — Alphabet raises 2026 capex guidance to $195–205B, spotlighting AI infrastructure spend
Oil price spike — Brent crude jumps 3.4% to $94/barrel, pressuring broader market

stocks.discussion_driver: Super Micro Computer surged ~25% on July 22 after releasing a preliminary fiscal Q4 update showing a record $60B+ order backlog and gross margins of 15-17% (roughly double prior guidance of 8.2-8.4%). An announced AI data center deal with SpaceX further validated SMCI as a critical AI infrastructure provider, though the stock remains 51% below its 52-week high amid ongoing governance questions.
bull_case: 70-80% market share in liquid-cooled AI racks with a $60B+ record order backlog and SpaceX AI data center deal validating tier-1 demand at the exact moment the industry is being forced to adopt liquid cooling
Gross margins recovering to 9.9% from 6.3% with management guiding to 15-17%, signaling a significant profitability inflection that could power shares back toward the analyst target zone
bear_case: Ongoing Board independent review tied to export-control matters creates governance overhang, compounded by CEO and director selling a combined 680K shares in May 2026
High cash burn ($6.6B operating cash outflow in fiscal Q3 FY2026) and $8.8B in total bank debt and convertibles limit financial flexibility if AI capex spending slows

stocks.discussion_driver: Alphabet beat Q2 2026 estimates with $119.8B in revenue and Google Cloud surging 82% YoY to $24.8B, but shares fell 4%+ after-hours when management raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B, well above the $188B analyst consensus. The elevated spending signals aggressive AI infrastructure commitment, sparking a bull-bear debate on whether it leads to durable competitive advantage or destroys near-term shareholder value.
bull_case: Google Cloud revenue surged 82% YoY to $24.8B in Q2 2026 with operating income tripling to $6.6B at a 32.9% margin, validating the AI infrastructure investment thesis with improving returns
Search revenue accelerating with AI Overviews driving 19% growth and 89% of analysts rating the stock Buy, reflecting broad institutional confidence in Alphabet's full-stack AI positioning
bear_case: 2026 capex guidance raised to $195-205B (above $188B consensus) is driving free cash flow negative, with 2027 capex expected to increase further, creating multi-year FCF margin compression
AI competitors OpenAI, Perplexity, and Microsoft threaten Google's core search dominance, while a $3.5B EU fine adds regulatory overhang to an already capital-intensive investment cycle

stocks.discussion_driver: Tesla reported Q2 2026 results showing a stark bifurcation: record $28.2B in revenue significantly beat the $26.4B estimate, but adjusted EPS of $0.33 missed the $0.54 consensus by 39% as operating profit fell 57% YoY and regulatory credits collapsed. Shares fell 5%+ after-hours, with bears focused on collapsing margins while bulls point to the dramatically improved cash burn rate and upcoming FSD/robotaxi catalysts.
bull_case: Record Q2 revenue of $28.2B beat estimates by 6.8%, and free cash flow burn of -$1.09B dramatically beat the -$3.64B estimate, signaling improving capital efficiency and operational execution

FSD, robotaxi, and Optimus robot represent unpriced optionality catalysts that could significantly re-rate shares if executed, with Wedbush maintaining a $600 price target on these platform opportunities
bear_case: Adjusted EPS of $0.33 missed the $0.54 consensus by 39%, with operating profit down 57% YoY as regulatory credit revenue collapsed and core auto margins deteriorated sharply
Trailing PE of 363x leaves no margin of safety if the robotaxi and FSD commercialization timeline slips further, with GLJ Research maintaining a Sell rating at $24.86

stocks.discussion_driver: IBM confirmed its Q2 2026 revenue miss ($17.16B vs $17.58B consensus) and lowered its full-year forecast at its July 22 earnings call, largely corroborating the July 14 preliminary warning that sent the stock crashing 25%+ in a single session — the worst one-day drop in company history. The EPS miss ($2.27 vs $2.97 expected) reflected enterprise AI budgets shifting toward cloud infrastructure hardware at the expense of IBM's software and services stack.
bull_case: Software segment continues to grow with the generative AI book of business exceeding $12.5B, and IBM has raised its dividend for 31 consecutive years, providing income support for investors weathering the selloff
Jefferies maintained a Buy rating (target $260) after the Q2 miss, suggesting analysts view the post-crash price near $213 as an attractive entry point relative to IBM's AI monetization trajectory
bear_case: Q2 revenue of $17.16B missed by $420M with full-year guidance cut, signaling structural headwinds as enterprises redirect AI spend toward cloud infrastructure hardware rather than IBM's software-centric stack
Down 35%+ from its June 2026 high near $332, with HSBC downgraded to Reduce at a $191 target and the worst single-session drop in IBM's trading history still fresh in institutional memory

stocks.discussion_driver: ServiceNow beat Q2 2026 estimates across the board (revenue $3.99B, subscription growth 23% YoY constant currency beating guidance by 1.5 points, operating margin 29.5% vs 26.5% guidance) and raised full-year subscription guidance to $15.76-15.78B for the second time, citing robust AI demand for Now Assist and AI Control Tower. Shares fell 6.47% during the regular July 22 session before rallying 4.68% after-hours on the results.
bull_case: AI Control Tower and Now Assist gaining rapid enterprise traction with AI ACV surpassing $1B and targeting $1.5B by year-end 2026, supporting the second upward revision to full-year subscription revenue guidance
Q2 subscription growth of 23% YoY constant currency beat guidance by 1.5 points with 29.5% operating margin (3 points above guidance), demonstrating strong pricing power and execution discipline
bear_case: At 61x trailing PE with the stock down 54% from its 52-week high, significant multiple contraction risk exists if OpenAI's new enterprise product Presence captures core IT service management market share
Armis integration adds a 200bps headwind to free cash flow margin and gross margin is under pressure from AI infrastructure scaling costs, introducing near-term integration and execution risk
